title: Why AI Startups Will Disappear Without Compute Markets — Evan Conrad, San Francisco Compute
talk_summary: This is a macro-finance talk about GPU compute markets, credit risk, and why AI labs need physically settled forward markets for clusters; it contains almost no engineering technique. The only transferable idea is a general principle about capacity planning and liquidity under demand uncertainty.

takeaways.technique: Capacity buffer via resale/liquidity instead of fixed provisioning
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue that buyers who over- or under-provision compute have no way to sell surplus or buy spot capacity, so they either waste money or fail; a liquid market lets you shed excess and cover shortfalls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's no way to sell your capacity to somebody else and there's no way to buy more capacity if you need it

takeaways.technique: Provision against measured demand, not guesses
takeaways.what_they_do: They note that predicting demand correctly is very low probability, so you end up way over- or under-provisioned with no escape valve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the likelihood that you predict your demand correctly is very low
